solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very clear signal needed after damaged canals are emptied

indicators.note: needed after says the signal word comes after the rearranged letters
damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so the canals letters plus the pair from are get rearranged
emptied means the word are loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: a whistle is a signal, as a referee's or a guard's

explanation.surface: Something broken in the canal system needs a clear warning sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps just the outer letters of 'are'; those two join the canals letters in the shuffle, and the signal is placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for spotless or completely free of fault, extended here to mean thoroughly clear.

clue.text: Musical city in romance novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of romance are made new in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A city famous for music features in a love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book the romance is in, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is famous for violin making by Stradivari, Amati and Guarneri, hence musical.

clue.text: Clubs put in correct order

indicators.note: put in tells us the clubs letter is placed inside the word for correct

parts.note: to correct text is to edit it
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are arranged in the proper sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree or command issued by authority is an order.

clue.text: Big cheese sandwich mainly found in new menu and old

indicators.note: found in says the trimmed sandwich word sits inside the other letters
new signals that the letters of menu are given a new order
mainly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a round is one sandwich, as in a round of ham sandwiches

explanation.surface: A huge cheese sandwich turns up on both the current and the former menu.
explanation.walkthrough: A round is one whole sandwich in British usage; 'mainly' drops its last letter before it goes inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for the most important person, the boss or top dog.

clue.text: Dubious conjecture in action one's dropped

indicators.note: in places the conjecture word inside the shortened action word
dropped says the one letter is removed from the word for action

parts.note: a suit is a legal action, a lawsuit
I is the Roman numeral for one
spec, short for speculation, is a conjecture

explanation.surface: Someone guesses doubtfully about an operation in which a person has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: SUIT with I 'dropped' leaves SUT; SPEC goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious is questionable and open to doubt, as a suspect claim is.

clue.text: Scots separatist with Ebenezer regularly welcoming father

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so the picked letters enclose the father letters
regularly means taking every other letter of Ebenezer

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A Scottish breakaway joins Ebenezer, who often welcomes a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking Ebenezer's odd letters 'regularly' gives EEEE, which is 'welcoming' FR in its middle. The Wee Frees are the Free Church of Scotland, which broke away in 1900 when the main body merged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickname for members of the Free Church of Scotland, a group that separated from the larger church.

clue.text: How 'facile' ends as 'vacuous'?

definitions.meaning: the word facile ends with a final letter E, read as a phrase of three words

explanation.surface: A question about whether the ending of a glib remark makes it empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a cryptic description: facile finishes 'in an E'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: silly and lacking sense, as in an empty-headed remark.

clue.text: Send a message to us

definitions.meaning: to wire a message by an electric signal system
the setter's own newspaper, in which the puzzle appears

explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the newspaper speaking of itself: this Toughie was printed in that daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to send by wire, and the name is the publishing daily newspaper.

clue.text: Adopt dialect primarily found in European language

indicators.note: found in puts the dialect letter inside the language word

parts.note: Norse is the language of medieval Scandinavia

indicators.note: primarily means first, so take the opening letter of dialect

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a regional speech found mainly in a Continental tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To back or approve a policy or candidate is to take it up as one's own.

clue.text: Posers like to hold a drink when reflecting

indicators.note: reflecting, as in a mirror, means the result is read backwards
to hold says the word for like encloses the drink

parts.note: same means alike, the like
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Models in a pose hold a glass while lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: SAME holding GIN gives SAMGINE, which 'when reflecting' reads backwards. 'reflecting' poses as thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Posers are puzzling questions, riddles hard to work out.

clue.text: Given power to arrest, Yorkshire Regional Crime Squad all finally going round

indicators.note: going round says the final letters surround the arrest word
all finally means the last letter of each of the four words

parts.note: to nab someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A regional police squad, authorised to make arrests, finally goes on patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters ('all finally') give ELED, 'going round' NAB.
explanation.definitionFit: To be authorised or made able to do something is to be empowered.

clue.text: Public regiment about to accept external cover-up?

parts.note: out means public, known to all, as a secret that is out

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the regiment letters are read backwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
to wear something is to tolerate or accept it, as in 'I won't wear that'

explanation.surface: A disgraced regiment is about to admit to a public scandal being covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RE into ER. The definition plays on 'cover-up' as clothing rather than concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes worn over everything else literally cover the body from outside.

clue.text: Keen backing music that's half-hearted

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the shortened music word is read in reverse
half-hearted means half the heart goes: of the double letter in the middle, one is lost

parts.note: reggae is Jamaican popular music

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for backing music which lacks conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of REGGAE's central pair of Gs to give REGAE, and 'backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being keen on something is being enthusiastic and impatient for it.

clue.text: A second weapons negotiation stopped by united attack

indicators.note: stopped by says the united letter plugs the middle of the talks word

parts.note: SALT, the Strategic Arms Limitation Talks between the US and USSR
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Arms talks are halted when the allied side attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a violent onslaught on a person or position.

clue.text: Account portrayed in New Testament

indicators.note: the letters of Testament are portrayed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A story told in the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' reads as the Bible, but 'New' is part of the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A written or spoken report of facts, as a witness gives to police, is an account.

clue.text: Final check — business is on target

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece being on another means it follows it

parts.note: an end is an aim or target, as in a means to an end
a game is a line of business, as in 'the antiques game'

explanation.surface: A final inspection: the company is on track to hit its goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The last phase of a chess match, where checkmate is delivered, is the final stage of play.

clue.text: Close-fitting clothing once worn by current entertaining couple

indicators.note: worn by places the current letters inside the old garment

parts.note: a doublet was a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Two performers dressed in period costume, in modern style.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of comedians or performers working together form a two-person act.

clue.text: Set against trifle having turned sour

parts.note: to trifle with something is to play with it
milk that has turned sour is off

explanation.surface: The dessert has been left out and the cream has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' poses as the pudding but is the verb, to toy with.
explanation.definitionFit: To play one person off against another is to pit them against each other.

clue.text: Saw one who verifies book

parts.note: a prover is someone who proves, verifying a claim

explanation.surface: A checker spotted a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a short traditional maxim.

clue.text: This would cover indecency in graphic image about flick

parts.note: fig is short for figure, an illustration in a book
to leaf through pages is to flick through them

explanation.surface: A rude scene in a film would need some censorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical statues and paintings traditionally hide nudity with a carefully placed plant cover.

clue.text: Violent criminal that's a difficult problem

definitions.meaning: a tough, a thug, here in a pet form
a hard question, as this newspaper series of harder puzzles is named

explanation.surface: A thug is a real headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal words for a hard nut and for a hard puzzle, the name of this very series.

clue.text: Dry T-shirt mangled by skivvy in the end

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
in the end means the last letter of skivvy

explanation.surface: A servant wrecks a shirt in the wringer, eventually getting it dry.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangle is an old wringer for laundry, and 'skivvy' is a menial servant, so the surface is a laundry scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry in the throat means wanting a drink.

clue.text: Maximum portion of text rememberable

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The largest possible chunk of a memorable passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe the furthest or highest degree, as in extreme or maximum pressure.

clue.text: Plain deliveries arriving with post, finally

indicators.note: arriving with says the final letter is attached alongside

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of post

explanation.surface: Plain parcels turn up in the mail at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' suggests mail, but it is the cricket bowling term.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plain to see, not hidden.

clue.text: Tried not to open treasure

indicators.note: not to open means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: strove means tried hard

explanation.surface: Someone tried not to unlock the treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' poses as the verb of the surface but is the fodder: STROVE minus its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a hoard of valuables, as in treasure trove.

clue.text: Fool tackling one English test, getting the bird

indicators.note: tackling means taking on, so the fool word grips the one letter

parts.note: to gull someone is to fool or dupe them
I is the Roman numeral for one
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK vehicles

explanation.surface: A clown attempts an English exam and is booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the bird' means being jeered, a British idiom, but here 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: Saying rather too much in a little while

indicators.note: in places the excess word inside the short time word

parts.note: mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'
OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: Someone talking a bit too much in a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A short maxim summing up a principle is a saying.

clue.text: The setter got picked up — not a pretty sight

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: the setter is I, and got in the sense of understood is saw

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler was collected and looked rather a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter' is the compiler speaking of themself, I; 'got' as in 'I get it' is 'saw'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building or object spoiling the view is unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Amaze, as Lennon and Led Zep do?

definitions.text: as Lennon and Led Zep do?
definitions.meaning: both names begin with the same two letters, L then E

explanation.surface: Rock stars like John Lennon and Led Zeppelin astonish their fans.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as START LE: both Lennon and Led Zep open with LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a sudden shock of surprise is to amaze someone.

clue.text: Cleopatra's caress causing flapping in the baths?

definitions.meaning: the Cleopatra is a species of yellow butterfly, so its caress is a butterfly's touch
a swimming style with both arms moving together, done at the public baths

explanation.surface: The Egyptian queen's touch made people flap at the bathhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleopatra is a butterfly species (Gonepteryx cleopatra), not only the queen. 'Baths' is the British word for a public swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming technique where both arms sweep over together, like wings.
